headline: Habagat Rains to Persist Across Luzon and Parts of Visayas on Sunday
seoTitle: Habagat Rains to Persist Sunday, August 30 | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA says Habagat will continue bringing monsoon rains to Metro Manila and several Luzon provinces on Sunday, with rain also affecting parts of Visayas.
keywords: Zambales Bataan Metro Manila rain forecast
deck: PAGASA forecasts monsoon rains over Metro Manila and several western and central Luzon provinces, with scattered rain also affecting Western Visayas and Negros Island Region.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Southwest Monsoon or Habagat will continue to bring rains over Luzon and parts of the Visayas on Sunday, August 30, according to PAGASA.
Monsoon rains are expected over Metro Manila, Ilocos Sur, Pangasinan, La Union, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac, Pampanga, Bulacan, Rizal and Cavite.

sections.heading: Other areas
paragraphs: Occasional rains are forecast over Ilocos Norte, Abra, Apayao, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Nueva Vizcaya, Nueva Ecija, Laguna, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro and Oriental Mindoro.
The rest of Luzon, Western Visayas and Negros Island Region are expected to have cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Communities that have already received prolonged rainfall remain vulnerable even when rain temporarily weakens. PAGASA has warned that accumulated rainfall can increase the risk of flooding and rain-induced landslides, particularly in saturated and low-lying areas.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: PAGASA's weekly outlook had already indicated that the August 29 to 30 period would remain wet as a low-pressure area east of Extreme Northern Luzon continued to enhance Habagat, even with a Philippine landfall considered less likely.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Residents should monitor PAGASA rainfall warnings and local disaster advisories because warning levels and affected areas can change quickly as rain bands move.
